title: Distributed Job Orchestration
summary: Scaled a job platform to 12M+ jobs/day.
problem: A central job platform was hitting throughput limits as volume grew into the millions of jobs per day; workers contended on the same tables and latency spiked under load.
approach: Partitioned the PostgreSQL job tables, moved processing to asynchronous workers, and made every job idempotent so retries were safe. Tuned batch sizes and back-pressure.
impact: 12M+ jobs/day with ~40% higher throughput and predictable latency, with failure recovery handled automatically instead of manually.

title: Multi-Bank HTTP Proxy
summary: Transparent tenant-aware routing to banks' LMS systems.
problem: Customer API traffic had to reach the correct bank's loan-management system, with clean tenant isolation.
approach: Built a transparent HTTP proxy that resolves the tenant from the MSISDN and routes traffic to the right bank's LMS, keeping the integration surface uniform.
impact: A single, maintainable entry point for multi-bank routing instead of bespoke per-bank integrations.

title: Financial Reconciliation Pipeline
problem: Reconciliation was slow and error-prone, and failures needed manual intervention — risky for financial data.
approach: Built idempotent reconciliation workflows with automated failure recovery, so re-runs converge to the same state and transient failures self-heal.
impact: 300K+ transactions/day reconciled automatically with far less manual effort and higher accuracy.

title: Credit-Rule Engine Refactor
summary: Cut rule execution from 9 hours to 2–3.
problem: The credit-rule engine took ~9 hours to run, blocking downstream processes and limiting how often rules could be evaluated.
approach: Introduced parallel processing and workload partitioning so independent rule sets run concurrently instead of sequentially.
impact: Execution dropped from 9 hours to 2–3 hours, unblocking more frequent runs.

title: Async Bulk Ingestion
summary: 1M+ row uploads via parallel, idempotent workers.
problem: Large data uploads (1M+ rows) had to process reliably without blocking the app or duplicating work when a batch was retried.
approach: Designed asynchronous bulk-ingestion workflows on RabbitMQ, Redis, and PostgreSQL — parallel workers, idempotent processing, and batched job execution so uploads run concurrently and can safely re-run.
impact: Supports 1M+ row uploads with parallel throughput and no duplicate side-effects on failure.

title: Consent Management Platform
problem: A platform for 2M+ users needed to track consent (opt-in/opt-out) with a complete, trustworthy history for regulatory audits.
approach: Modelled consent with a current-state table for fast live reads plus an append-only audit-history table, so every opt-in/opt-out change is traceable for compliance.
impact: 2M+ users' consent tracked with audit-ready history that stands up to regulatory review.
